claims.finding: Mama's Creations priced a 5.6m-share spot secondary at $18.00 on 2026-06-30 (range $17.50-18.50, William Blair and DA Davidson joint books), the stock fell 12.3% on the announcement, and it now enters the print at $15.96 - 11.3% below the price every institution in that deal paid nine weeks ago - with roughly $100m of undeployed cash and the acquisition the raise was understood to fund still unannounced.

claims.why_not_priced: The offering is wire copy; the position of the deal buyers is not, and nothing in the capture computes it. A freshly placed institutional book sitting 11% underwater into the first print since the raise is the marginal holder, and the reason the price fell 12.8% over twenty sessions with, in the corpus's own words on 2026-08-27, 'can't find a reason for the drop'. There is no news-search coverage of this ticker at all (n_queries=0 in every sweep), so no preview links the raise, the undeployed cash and the print.

claims.finding: An 8-K with items 1.01, 8.01 and 9.01 - a material definitive agreement plus other events - was filed on 2026-07-01, the day after the offering closed, and its contents appear nowhere in the 57-item capture; nine weeks later the retail base is still 'waiting for the big news on the company's next acquisitions'.
claims.corpus_ref: filings.json, 8-K dated 2026-07-01 with items '1.01,8.01,9.01'; docs/170806f7b3373558655fba2c2c0b8739efd7da18.txt entry dated 2026-07-08T20:02:36Z
claims.why_not_priced: The body is not stored and no observed source describes it, so the market's read of what was signed the day after a $100m raise is invisible in this corpus. An item 1.01 filed into that sequence is most naturally a purchase agreement or a credit facility, either of which would be reported on and quantified at this print. The direction is uncertain, which is why the range is wide, but the existence of an undescribed material agreement immediately after the raise is a fact the previews cannot have weighed because there are no previews.
